title: Central Bank of India - 532885 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Central Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 13.26% to ₹1,324 crore, with advances up 28.58% YoY and gross NPA at 2.60%.
summary.overview: Central Bank of India reported Q1 FY27 global business of ₹833,320 crore (up 18.29% YoY), with deposits up 11.68% to ₹478,972 crore and gross advances up 28.58% to ₹354,348 crore. Net profit rose 13.26% to ₹1,324 crore, NIM was 3.06%, and ROE improved to 14.92% from 14.17%. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.60% (down 53 bps YoY), net NPA at 0.49%, and slippage ratio at 0.29%. Management said the quarter's advances growth was driven partly by a low base in corporate loans, and quarter-on-quarter advances growth was only about 2.85%. Liquidity coverage ratio fell sharply from 235% to 156%, as the bank deployed liquidity into loans.

financial_highlights.value: ₹276 crore (per Q&A); ₹621 crore vs ₹353 crore in segment comments

segments.name: Retail (RAM)
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 23.92% to ₹1,05,523 crore. Segment profit was reported at ₹1,377 crore vs ₹633 crore a year earlier in an analyst's reading of segment data.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 21.14% to ₹64,274 crore. Gold loan book is ₹36,000 crore; gold loans under agriculture are MCLR-linked, retail gold loans are not.

segments.name: Corporate credit
segments.commentary: Corporate credit rose 46.52% to ₹1,12,770 crore from ₹76,966 crore, on a low base. Growth is concentrated in renewable energy, data centres, HAM projects and CRE. RAM-to-corporate mix is 68:32 against a 65:35 guidance (±5%).

segments.name: Wholesale and unallocated
segments.commentary: An analyst cited wholesale segment at minus ₹139 crore (vs ₹284 crore) and unallocated at minus ₹75 crore (vs ₹322 crore). Management said provisioning had not risen and did not clearly explain the change.

segments.name: Insurance associates
segments.commentary: Bank holds about 26% in Generali Central Life and Generali Central Non-Life, with ₹627 crore invested in total. Management expects higher income from both this year after the establishment phase.

guidance_outlook: Deposit growth guidance of 11% to 12% and advances growth guidance of 14% to 16% for FY27, which management said it will align with in the current quarter.
Quarter-on-quarter advances growth of about 3% expected to continue.
NIM guided at 3% and above; ROA guided at 1% and above.
Cost-to-income ratio to fall by 1.5% to 1.6% in the coming year, against a target below 56%.
Yield on advances expected to rise from 7.89% to about 8% by March 2027, led by gold loan and SHG yields of 8%+.

ECL transition planned from 1 April 2027; management estimated about 80 bps CRAR impact if provisioning is spread over five years or taken at once. Total ECL requirement estimated at ₹4,500-5,000 crore, with ₹1,525 crore already provided for Stage 1 and 2.
Technical write-off recoveries targeted at ₹2,200-2,500 crore for FY27; 600-700 property sales targeted against 460 last year.
FCNR(B) mobilisation target of USD400 million by September 2026 (USD8.4 million mobilised so far).
GIFT City targets: deposits of USD200 million and trade book of USD500 million over the next few years.
capex_capacity: Network of 4,605 branches (65% rural and semi-urban), 3,820 ATMs, 13,890 BC outlets, 30 BC MaXX centres and 1 IFSC Banking Unit; 22,346 total touch points.
New branch opened at GIFT City, Gandhinagar on 29 June 2026.
Plans to open more corporate finance and mid-corporate branches.
Around 1,000 credit officers in specialised training to join in the first week of October 2026 for deployment at credit centres.
300 marketing officers hired and posted; 35 customer acquisition centres and 9 government business centres opened.
Board has approved establishing wealth management, credit card, NRI and marketing verticals; credit card entry is being initiated.
demand_pricing: Retail, agriculture and MSME growth of about 24%, 21% and 18% respectively; management expects similar rates ahead.
Growth engines named as gold loans and SHG, with dedicated divisions reporting to an Executive Director; South India cited as a gold-loan opportunity.
Deposit products: Cent Queen mobilised ₹1,457 crore and Salary Cent Prestige ₹787 crore.
Term deposits grew about 12%; around 85% of deposits are under ₹3 crore.
ECLGS 5.0: 34,824 applications sanctioned for ₹4,646 crore; guarantees issued in 30,561 accounts for ₹4,353 crore; disbursed in 27,567 accounts for ₹3,693 crore.
Business per branch ₹185 crore; business per employee ₹24 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is capital raising planned, given the Board's approval of up to about ₹7,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CRAR of 18.28% and CET1 of 16.24% are sufficient for guidance, so no capital raise is planned currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LCR fall from 235% to 156% and NSFR from 147% to 128%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excess liquidity carries a cost and has been deployed; CD ratio rose from 64% to 74%. It said LCR remains above the regulatory threshold.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments drive the 28.6% advances growth, and what protects underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate grew 46.52% from a low base. Management cited a 0.29% slippage ratio, or 0.19% excluding agriculture KCC slippage of ₹200 crore, and better post-disbursement monitoring.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for deposit repricing and FCNR mobilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Term deposits are largely repriced at a 4.60% cost of deposits. FCNR(B) mobilisation is USD8.4 million so far, with a USD400 million target by September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Average yield on the corporate book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have corporate yield data; overall yield on advances is 7.89%, up from 7.78%, and is expected to reach about 8% by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost-to-income fall below 56%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited income steps (forex and BG cells, exporter meets, insurance and LC/BG business) and cost cuts (cash retention, ATM and currency chest use, utilities), targeting a 1.5-1.6% reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for credit cards and GIFT City?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit card and wealth management verticals were approved by the Board. GIFT City targets USD200 million deposits and USD500 million trade book over several years; about ₹470 crore has been disbursed there.

risks_watch: Liquidity coverage ratio fell to 156% from 235%, and NSFR to 128% from 147%; watch for further decline as the CD ratio rises.
ECL transition from 1 April 2027 needs about ₹4,500-5,000 crore in provisioning, with about ₹1,525 crore already provided.
Corporate book concentration: corporate loans up 46.52% in a single year, so underwriting quality needs testing.
Treasury income of ₹276 crore is lower YoY on market conditions.
Segment profit data conflicts with management's explanation; the wholesale and unallocated swing was not clearly explained.
Recovery targets depend on technical write-off recoveries of ₹2,200-2,500 crore and property sales.
summary.management_tone: Confident and assertive on growth, capital and asset quality. Management was less precise on specific figures such as corporate yield and segment profit changes, and on the segment question it deflected to “provisioning has come down.”
key_quotes: Growth is not a challenge for Central Bank of India now. We have enough capital. We have enough resources and the momentum and credit underwriting quality, post disbursement monitoring part, all these things we have taken care of.

So, comfort of having 215% and having CD ratio of 66% or 64% for any vibrant organization and growing organization, it is liability because those high-quality liquid assets and all those things comes with a cost.

adds.what: New branch at GIFT City, Gandhinagar opened 29 June 2026 (already opened)
Plans to open more corporate finance and mid-corporate branches (no number or timing given)
Around 1,000 credit officers joining credit centres (personnel, not productive capacity) in October 2026

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 14-16% advances growth and 11-12% deposit growth was held, backed partly by ~24%/21%/18% retail/agri/MSME growth, gold loan and SHG engines, and a new ~1,000 credit officer deployment, but no specific new capacity or order book was quantified and QoQ advances growth of only ~2.85% against ~3% guidance raises execution questions.
